title: Defining Relative Clauses: who, which, that, whose, where, when
grammarTitle: Defining Relative Clauses — Identifying Which One
grammarNote: Определительные придаточные предложения (defining relative clauses) отвечают на вопрос «который именно?» — они необходимы для понимания смысла предложения. Без них предложение становится неполным или неоднозначным. Запятые НЕ используются. На B1 уровне важно правильно выбирать relative pronoun и понимать, когда его можно опустить.

grammarTable.subject: WHO
grammarTable.example: "The student WHO passed the exam was happy." / "The people WHO helped me."

grammarTable.subject: WHOM
grammarTable.example: "The lecturer WHOM I admire most." (formal) / "the person WHOM she met."

grammarTable.subject: WHICH
grammarTable.example: "The book WHICH changed my mind." / "The city WHICH she was born in."

grammarTable.subject: THAT
grammarTable.example: "The student THAT passed." / "The book THAT changed my mind."

grammarTable.subject: WHOSE
grammarTable.example: "The student WHOSE essay won." / "The building WHOSE windows were broken."

grammarTable.subject: WHERE
grammarTable.example: "The library WHERE I study." / "The city WHERE she grew up."

grammarTable.subject: WHEN
grammarTable.example: "The year WHEN she graduated." / "The moment WHEN I understood."

grammarExtra.title: Omitting the relative pronoun — when is it possible?

rows.form: OBJECT clauses: pronoun CAN be omitted
rows.example: "The book [that/which] she wrote." = "The book she wrote." ✅ (she = subject; book = object → omit pronoun)

rows.form: SUBJECT clauses: pronoun CANNOT be omitted
rows.example: "The book that changed her life." ✗ "The book changed her life." — (book is the subject of "changed" — need pronoun) ✅

rows.form: Test: is there a subject after the pronoun?
rows.example: "The book [that] she wrote" → she = subject ✅ CAN omit. "The book that changed her life" → no other subject. CANNOT omit. ✅

rows.form: WHOSE and WHERE cannot be omitted
rows.example: "The student whose essay won." ✅ / "The place where they met." ✅ — cannot omit whose or where. ✅
"The scientist WHO discovered penicillin." ✅ (preferred in formal writing)
"The scientist THAT discovered penicillin." ✅ (acceptable, especially in speech)
"She is the best researcher THAT the department has ever had." ✅ ("that" very natural here)
"He is the only student THAT has passed all modules." ✅
"The city WHERE I was born." ✅ / "The room WHERE we met." ✅
"The city WHICH she was born IN." ✅ / "The room IN WHICH we met." ✅ (formal)
"The country IN WHICH she lived for twenty years." ✅ = "the country WHERE she lived." ✅
"The moment AT WHICH she decided." / "The event AT WHICH they met." ✅ (formal writing)
"The student WHOSE essay won first prize." = the student's essay. ✅
"The building WHOSE architect won an award." ✅ / "The company WHOSE profits have increased." ✅
"The student whose essay won." ✗ "The student essay won." — CANNOT omit whose. ✅
"The report, the conclusions OF WHICH were disputed..." = "the report whose conclusions were disputed." ✅
✅ "The scientist WHO discovered penicillin." — remove "he": the relative pronoun IS the subject. ✅
✅ "The place WHICH she visited." — "what" is NOT a relative pronoun (for clauses only). ✅
✅ "The building WHOSE windows broke." — possessive = "whose," not "which + possessive." ✅
✅ "The year WHEN I graduated." — time → "when," not "where." ✅

grammarTip:
Defining Relative Clauses — NO commas:

WHO → people (subject)
"The student WHO passed."

WHOM → people (object, formal)
"The professor WHOM I admire."

WHICH → things/animals
"The book WHICH changed my mind."

THAT → people or things (can replace who/which)
"The student THAT passed." / "The book THAT changed."

WHOSE → possession
"The student WHOSE essay won."

WHERE → places
"The city WHERE she grew up."

WHEN → times
"The year WHEN she graduated."

Omitting the pronoun (object position only):
"The book [that] she wrote." ✅ (she = subject after pronoun)
"The book that changed her life." ✅ (CANNOT omit — no other subject)

⚠️ Errors:
✗ who HE discovered → ✅ who discovered
✗ the place what → ✅ the place which/where
✗ the year where → ✅ the year when

exercises.text: "The student ___ won the prize was from Almaty."
exercises.hint: People → WHO (subject). "The student WHO won the prize." ✅

exercises.text: "She lost the report ___ she had been writing all week."
exercises.hint: Things → WHICH or THAT. "The report THAT she had been writing." ✅ (object position — could also omit)

exercises.text: "The city ___ I was born has changed a lot."
exercises.hint: Place → WHERE. "The city WHERE I was born." ✅

exercises.text: "I met a researcher ___ work has been published in Nature."
exercises.hint: "whose work" = the researcher's work (possessive). "A researcher WHOSE work has been published." ✅

exercises.text: "The book that I read last week was excellent." — Can "that" be omitted?
opts: Yes — "I" is the subject; "that" = object → can omit
exercises.correct: Yes — "I" is the subject; "that" = object → can omit
exercises.hint: "I" is the subject after "that" → "that" = object → CAN omit. "The book I read last week." ✅

exercises.text: "The book that changed her life." — Can "that" be omitted?
opts: No — there's no other subject; "that" is the subject of "changed"
exercises.correct: No — there's no other subject; "that" is the subject of "changed"
exercises.hint: "that" = subject of "changed" → CANNOT omit. "The book changed her life." would be a different sentence. ✅

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct relative pronoun for time.
exercises.text: "The moment ___ I understood English was in my second year."
exercises.hint: Time → WHEN. "The moment WHEN I understood English." ✅

exercises.text: "The scientist who he discovered radium won a Nobel Prize."
opts: "who he" is wrong — remove "he": the relative pronoun IS the subject
exercises.correct: "who he" is wrong — remove "he": the relative pronoun IS the subject
exercises.hint: ✅ "The scientist WHO discovered radium." — remove "he." "Who" IS the subject. ✅

exercises.text: "The place ___ she grew up was a small village."
exercises.hint: Place → WHERE. NOT "what" (which is not a relative pronoun). "The place WHERE she grew up." ✅

exercises.text: "She is the most talented student ___ I have ever taught."
exercises.hint: "...the most talented student WHO/THAT I have ever taught." — both correct; "that" is very natural after superlatives. ✅

exercises.text: "The university ___ she studied was founded in 1958." (formal version with preposition)
exercises.hint: "where she studied" ✅ (natural) / "at which she studied" ✅ (formal) / "which she studied at" ✅ (informal with hanging prep). All natural. ✅

exercises.text: "The building which its roof was damaged has been repaired."
opts: "which its roof" should be "whose roof" — possessive = whose
exercises.correct: "which its roof" should be "whose roof" — possessive = whose
exercises.hint: ✅ "The building WHOSE ROOF was damaged." — possessive: "whose," not "which + possessive pronoun." ✅

exercises.text: "The professor ___ I admire most has just published a new book." (formal)
exercises.hint: Formal: "the professor WHOM I admire" (object = whom). Informal: "the professor WHO I admire" also acceptable. ✅

exercises.text: "The year ___ she won the scholarship was the turning point in her career."
exercises.hint: "The year WHEN she won the scholarship." — time → WHEN. ✅

exercises.text: "He is the only student ___ has submitted on time."
exercises.hint: "the only student WHO/THAT has submitted." — both work; "that" is very natural after "the only." ✅

exercises.instruction: What does "where" replace in formal English?
exercises.text: "The laboratory where she worked" = "the laboratory ___ she worked."
opts: Both "in which" and "at which" are possible depending on context
exercises.correct: Both "in which" and "at which" are possible depending on context
exercises.hint: "In which she worked" (worked in the lab) ✅ / "at which she worked" (worked at the lab) ✅ — depends on the preposition. ✅

opts: Never have commas — they are essential for meaning
questions.correct: Never have commas — they are essential for meaning
questions.hint: Defining = no commas. The clause is ESSENTIAL for identifying the noun. ✅

questions.text: "The book that she wrote" — can "that" be omitted?
opts: Yes — "she" is the subject; "that" = object → can omit
questions.correct: Yes — "she" is the subject; "that" = object → can omit
questions.hint: "she" follows "that" = she is the subject. "That" = object position → can omit. "The book she wrote." ✅

questions.text: "The book that changed her mind" — can "that" be omitted?
questions.hint: "That" = subject of "changed" → CANNOT omit. No other subject follows. ✅

questions.text: "The student ___ essay won is from Karagandy." (possessive)

questions.hint: "WHEN" after time nouns (year, moment, day, time). ✅

opts: "What" is not a relative pronoun — should be "which" or "that"
questions.correct: "What" is not a relative pronoun — should be "which" or "that"
questions.hint: ✅ "The place WHICH she visited." / "The place THAT she visited." — "what" = NOT a relative pronoun. ✅

questions.text: "The scientist who discovered X" vs "The scientist that discovered X":
opts: Both are correct; "who" is preferred in formal writing
questions.correct: Both are correct; "who" is preferred in formal writing
questions.hint: "Who" preferred for people (formal). "That" also acceptable, especially in speech. ✅

questions.text: "In which" is the formal equivalent of:
questions.hint: "The room IN WHICH we met." = "The room WHERE we met." ✅ "In which" = formal "where." ✅

questions.text: "The building whose windows broke." — whose here:
opts: Shows possession: the windows belong to the building
questions.correct: Shows possession: the windows belong to the building
questions.hint: "WHOSE" = possessive relative, for people AND things. The windows are the building's. ✅

questions.text: When is "that" especially natural in a defining clause?
opts: After superlatives ("the best that...") and "the only"
questions.correct: After superlatives ("the best that...") and "the only"
questions.hint: "The best student THAT the department has had." / "The only one THAT passed." — "that" very natural. ✅

questions.text: "The scientist who he discovered radium." — Error:
opts: Remove "he" — the relative pronoun IS the subject; "he" creates a double subject
questions.correct: Remove "he" — the relative pronoun IS the subject; "he" creates a double subject
questions.hint: ✅ "The scientist WHO discovered radium." — "who" = subject. Don't add "he." ✅

questions.text: "Whose" differs from other relative pronouns because:
opts: It shows possession and links noun to what belongs to it
questions.correct: It shows possession and links noun to what belongs to it
questions.hint: "Whose" = possessive. "The student WHOSE essay won." = the student's essay. ✅
